concept.title: List Paragraphs
concept.abstract: This section covers List Paragraphs in DOCX— the primary structure for presenting discrete, parallel items in a defined or co-equal sequence — and introduces two subsections: Ordered Lists and Unordered Lists. The converter reads the list type, nesting level, and topic context to determine whether to map each list to <ol>, <ul>, <steps>, <substeps>, <choices>, or <dl> in the DITA output.

conbody.p: List paragraphs communicate sequences, collections, and term-definition pairs that prose paragraphs cannot organise with equal clarity. They are the primary structure for presenting discrete, parallel items — steps in a procedure, items in a requirements checklist, and options in a configuration section.
A list communicates to the reader that its items share a structural relationship: either sequence matters and the order is meaningful, or the items are co-equal and interchangeable in position.
In a .docx file, list items are created using the built-in list controls:

ul.li: Home → Bullets – Considered as an unordered list.
Home → Numbering – Considered as an ordered list.

conbody.p: The converter maps ordered lists to <ol><li> and unordered lists to <ul><li> by default, then applies content pattern recognition based on topic type — an ordered list under an action-verb heading in a Task topic maps to <steps><step><cmd> instead.
conbody.note:
List paragraphs created by manually typing hyphens, asterisks, numbers, or bullet characters as Normal-styled paragraphs do not carry the List Paragraph style. Manually typed symbols produce plain

elements in the DITA output — no list structure is generated.
